name: Shankar Parida/ଶଙ୍କର ପରିଡା

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Shankar Parida’s Odia poem “ଦୀପାବଳି” brings an invocation to the ancestors into conversation with Jagannath. Repeated calls to come out of darkness gather memories of devotion, human failure and the speaker’s own incompleteness. The poem’s insistent rhythm makes the appeal feel both ceremonial and deeply personal.

At the temple steps, light becomes an offering and a request for an answer. Ancestors and descendants enter the same imaginative gathering, while the speaker asks the deity to emerge from concealment. The ending seeks an end to the journey through darkness, carrying the poem’s festival setting towards a wider longing for renewal.
